summary: A 7-year-old boy with a 3-week history of periorbital edema and frothy urine. Urinalysis shows heavy proteinuria without hematuria, and serum albumin is low.

documents.text: Male. DOB 2019-05-20. Guardian: mother. Nationality: South Korea.

Pediatric nephrology. 7-yo boy, 3 wks of puffy eyes in the morning, now ankle swelling; mother notes foamy urine. Recent URI 1 month ago. PMH atopic dermatitis. Wt 26.4 kg (baseline 24 kg). BP 104/66. Periorbital and pitting pedal edema, mild ascites. No rash, no joint pain.

Urinalysis: protein 4+, blood negative, RBC 0-2/HPF. Urine protein/creatinine ratio 6.8 mg/mg. Serum albumin 1.7 g/dL; total cholesterol 382 mg/dL; creatinine 0.38 mg/dL; C3 118 mg/dL (normal); ANA negative; hepatitis B sAg negative.

Imp: idiopathic nephrotic syndrome, presumed minimal change disease (age, no hematuria, normal C3, normal renal function). Biopsy not indicated now. Start prednisolone 60 mg/m2/day. Varicella IgG positive. Diet: no added salt.
Prednisolone 50 mg PO daily (60 mg/m2), dispensed 28 days.
Urine dipstick protein trace. Urine protein/creatinine ratio 0.4 mg/mg. Serum albumin 2.6 g/dL.

Pediatric nephrology follow-up, comprehensive H&P. 7-yo boy, day 15 of daily prednisolone for idiopathic nephrotic syndrome, presumed minimal change disease.

HPI: Presented 09-14 with 3 wks of periorbital and then pedal edema and foamy urine, after a URI about 1 month earlier. UPCR 6.8, albumin 1.7, cholesterol 382, C3 normal, ANA negative, HBsAg negative, creatinine 0.38. Started prednisolone 50 mg daily (60 mg/m2) on 09-16 without biopsy. Mother reports urine is no longer foamy, and the morning eye puffiness and ankle swelling resolved over the last week. Appetite increased, and he is a bit more irritable and sleeps less well. No fever, vomiting, abdominal pain, gross hematuria, or decreased urine output. Mother has been checking home dipsticks: negative to trace for the last 4 days. 09-29: dipstick trace, UPCR 0.4, albumin 2.6.

VITALS: Ht 122 cm (~45th percentile), Wt 24.6 kg (~45th percentile; 26.4 kg on 09-14 with edema, baseline 24 kg), BMI 16.5 kg/m2 (~70th percentile). BP 106/64 (~75th-90th percentile for age/height), HR 84, RR 20, Temp 36.8 C, SpO2 99% RA.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
- Atopic dermatitis, dx 2021, mild, intermittent flares of the antecubital and popliteal areas
- Idiopathic nephrotic syndrome, dx 09/2026 (this episode)
No other cardiac, pulmonary, hepatic, renal, autoimmune, endocrine or neurologic history. No prior thromboembolism, no prior serious infections, no malignancy.

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY: None.

ALLERGIES: NKDA. No food allergy.

MEDICATIONS (reconciled):
- Prednisolone 50 mg PO daily, started 2026-09-16 (dispensed 28 days)
- Emollient (fragrance-free moisturizer) BID to skin, since 2021
- Hydrocortisone 1% cream PRN for eczema flares, since 2021; not used in the last 2 weeks
Recently stopped: none. No NSAIDs, no antibiotics, no supplements.

IMMUNIZATIONS: Up to date per mother. Varicella IgG positive (09-16).

SOCIAL HISTORY: Lives with both parents and one younger sister, 2nd grade, attends school (currently home during initial treatment). No tobacco smoke exposure at home. No alcohol or substances (age-appropriate). Diet low added salt.

FAMILY HISTORY: No kidney disease, nephrotic syndrome or autoimmune disease; mother with seasonal allergic rhinitis.

ROS: Constitutional: increased appetite, mild irritability and sleep disturbance, no fever or weight loss. Eyes/ENT: no swelling now, no sore throat. Resp: no cough, dyspnea. CV: no chest pain, palpitations. GI: no abdominal pain, vomiting, diarrhea, melena. GU: no dysuria, gross hematuria, foamy urine now. MSK: no joint pain or swelling, no leg pain. Skin: dry patches on elbow creases, no rash otherwise. Neuro: no headache, visual change, or seizures. Heme: no easy bruising, no unilateral leg swelling.

PHYSICAL EXAM: Well appearing, active, in no distress. Mild rounding of the face, no other cushingoid features. No periorbital edema. Oropharynx clear. Neck supple, no lymphadenopathy. Heart RRR, normal S1/S2, no murmur. Lungs clear bilaterally, no increased work of breathing. Abdomen soft, non-tender, no ascites on exam, no hepatosplenomegaly. Extremities: no pitting edema of the ankles or sacrum, no calf tenderness or asymmetry, cap refill <2 s. Skin: few dry eczematous patches in the antecubital fossae, no excoriation or secondary infection. Neuro: age-appropriate, normal gait.

NEPHROTIC SYNDROME ASSESSMENT:
- Edema: resolved. Weight back to baseline (26.4 -> 24.6 kg).
- Proteinuria trend: UPCR 6.8 (09-14) -> 0.4 (09-29); dipstick 4+ -> trace. Remission reached within about 2 weeks of steroids (steroid-sensitive course). Relapses: 0.
- Serum albumin 1.7 -> 2.6 g/dL (09-29); cholesterol 382 on 09-14, repeat today.
- Renal function normal (Cr 0.38 on 09-14). BP normal. No hematuria. No documented complications (no thrombosis, no infection).
- Steroid side effects so far: increased appetite, mood and sleep change, mild facial rounding.

ASSESSMENT/PLAN:
1. Idiopathic nephrotic syndrome, presumed minimal change disease, steroid-responsive, in remission on day 15 of daily prednisolone. Continue prednisolone 50 mg daily to complete the daily course, then taper to alternate-day dosing per protocol. Biopsy still not indicated.
2. Repeat panel and urinalysis drawn today. Continue home first-morning dipstick log daily; call for 2+ protein or more for 3 days, edema, fever or abdominal pain. Keep no-added-salt diet and avoid NSAIDs. Counsel on infection precautions and exposure to chickenpox.
3. Atopic dermatitis stable, continue emollients. Monitor BP, weight, mood, and growth on steroids.
Return to clinic in 2 weeks.

- Carvedilol 6.25 mg PO BID (since 2026-07, for small varices)

GI: no abdominal pain, nausea, melena, hematemesis, change in bowel habit; appetite good. GU: no hematuria. Heme: no easy bruising, no epistaxis. Neuro: no confusion, sleep reversal or tremor. Skin: no jaundice or pruritus. MSK: no bone pain. Psych: negative.

VITALS: Ht 175 cm, Wt 76 kg (stable vs. prior), BMI 24.8. BP 124/76, HR 62, Temp 36.7 C, RR 14, SpO2 98% on room air.

PHYSICAL EXAM:
General: well appearing, no distress.
HEENT: anicteric sclerae, moist mucosa.
Neck: no lymphadenopathy.
CV: regular rate and rhythm, no murmur.
Lungs: clear bilaterally.

Ext: no edema.
Skin: a few spider angiomata on upper chest, no jaundice.
Neuro: alert, oriented, no asterixis.

OBJECTIVE ASSESSMENT:
- ECOG performance status 0
- Stage: HCC BCLC B (multifocal, confined to right lobe, no macrovascular invasion, no extrahepatic disease); residual viable disease after 2 TACE
- Child-Pugh A6 (bilirubin 1.4, albumin 3.4, INR 1.17, no ascites, no encephalopathy); ALBI grade 2
- AFP 305 ng/mL on 2026-09-14 (288 on 2026-08-20; 412 at diagnosis)
- HBV DNA not detected on entecavir
- Varices: small, no red signs, EGD 2026-07
- Labs 2026-09-14 reviewed: plt 88, creatinine 0.9, ALT 41, AST 52

2. Small esophageal varices: continue carvedilol 6.25 mg BID; EGD was 2026-07, repeat if systemic therapy including an anti-VEGF agent is chosen and the interval is longer than 6 months.
3. HBV cirrhosis: continue entecavir 0.5 mg daily; HBV DNA undetectable. Continue 3-monthly AFP and liver panel.
4. Return in 2 weeks with tumor board recommendation; repeat imaging in 8-12 weeks.
Patient confirms no alcohol since the cirrhosis diagnosis. Denies any prior systemic therapy for liver cancer. Willing to travel to Seoul for study visits.

documents.text: Male. DOB 1952-11-09. Retired engineer. Nationality: South Korea.

Underwent pars plana vitrectomy with gas tamponade OD. Apixaban held 48 h pre-op per cardiology, resumed post-op day 1. Positioning instructions given.
Post-op day 4. Retina attached. VA OD hand motions (gas-filled). IOP 18. Continue drops.
